findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0355: References to Unauthorized Database Access through Content Providers
findings.explanation:
A content provider is exported with no permission: any installed app can query it. If it is public by design, accept it with a reason.
sync/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: provider app.pennyjar.sync.ReceiptsProvider; exported: yes (android:exported is set)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0357: References to Oversharing of File-Based Content Providers
findings.explanation:
A content provider is exported with no permission: any installed app can query it. If it is public by design, accept it with a reason.
sync/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: provider app.pennyjar.sync.ReceiptsProvider; exported: yes (android:exported is set)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0364: Exported And Unprotected Activities That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity is exported without a permission and loads any caller-supplied URL into a WebView whose JS bridge returns the session token, so any app can exfiltrate the token. Ward's analyzer said: Exported activities without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:32: HelpActivity exported with no permission.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:40: Trusts caller-supplied URL.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpBridge.kt:14: Session token exposed to the loaded page.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:30: activity .help.HelpActivity; exported: yes (android:exported is set); deep link schemes: pennyjar

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0327: References to APIs for Event-Bound Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
The app lock calls BiometricPrompt.authenticate without a CryptoObject and no key uses setUserAuthenticationRequired, so unlocking relies only on the callback.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/BiometricGate.kt:51: Event-bound authenticate without CryptoObject.

findings.title: MASWE-0042: Latest Platform Version Not Targeted
findings.explanation:
targetSdk is 34. Since 2026-08-31, Google Play accepts new phone and tablet apps and updates only if they target API 36 or higher (rule checked 2026-11-23).
app/build.gradle.kts:14: targetSdk 34

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0272: Identify Dependencies with Known Vulnerabilities in the Android Project
findings.explanation:
com.google.code.gson:gson:2.8.5 is in the affected range of 1 OSV advisory: GHSA-4jrv-ppp4-jm57/CVE-2022-25647. OSV Maven data downloaded 2026-11-26T21:30:18.923Z (published Mon, 23 Nov 2026 21:33:52 GMT). 9 of the other dependencies with exact versions match no OSV advisory, but 2 declarations have no version Ward can read (see evidence). Check those, and transitive dependencies, with a Gradle-aware scanner. OSV Maven data downloaded 2026-11-26T21:30:18.923Z (published Mon, 23 Nov 2026 21:33:52 GMT).
gradle/libs.versions.toml:11: version 2.8.5
sync/build.gradle.kts:37: implementation (catalog libs.gson) in module sync
app/build.gradle.kts:45: androidx.compose.ui:ui: no version (a BOM or constraint may set it)
app/build.gradle.kts:46: androidx.compose.material3:material3: no version (a BOM or constraint may set it)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0339: SQL Injection in Content Providers
findings.explanation:
The exported ReceiptsProvider passes the URI's last path segment into a raw SQL string with no parameterization.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ReceiptsProvider.kt:40: Untrusted path segment from caller URI.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ReceiptQueries.kt:20: Concatenated into rawQuery.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0394: Missing Input Validation in Custom URL Scheme Handlers
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity reads the 'page' query parameter from the pennyjar://help deep link and loads it in a JS-enabled WebView with no scheme or host allowlist.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:40: URL parameter taken from the deep link.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:43: Used directly as the WebView URL without validation.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0398: References to WebViewClient URL Loading Handlers
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity sets a default WebViewClient with no URL interception, so the JS-bridged WebView navigates to any site, including attacker pages reached from the deep-link URL.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:27: WebViewClient without shouldOverrideUrlLoading allowlist.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0204: Insecure Random API Usage
findings.explanation:
ShareLinks generates the share-link access token with java.util.Random, a predictable PRNG.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/share/ShareLinks.kt:11: Non-cryptographic PRNG.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/share/ShareLinks.kt:15: Used to build the share-link token.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0232: Broken Symmetric Encryption Modes
findings.explanation:
NoteCipher encrypts users' private notes with AES in ECB mode.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteCipher.kt:9: ECB transformation used for note encryption.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0207: Runtime Storage of Unencrypted Data in the App Sandbox
findings.explanation:
The account password is written unencrypted to the app sandbox (SharedPreferences).
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/CredentialStore.kt:12: Plaintext password persisted in the sandbox.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0208: Insufficient Key Sizes
findings.explanation:
The note encryption key is a 16-byte (128-bit) AES key, below the size MASTG requires; the Keystore key is 256-bit.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:13: AES key built from the 16 bytes on lines 8-11 (128-bit).

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0212: Use of Hardcoded Cryptographic Keys in Code
findings.explanation:
NoteKeys builds an AES SecretKeySpec from a hardcoded byte array, used by NoteCipher to encrypt users' private notes.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:8: Key bytes hardcoded in source.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:13: Hardcoded bytes turned into the note encryption key.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0287: Runtime Storage of Unencrypted Data via the SharedPreferences API
findings.explanation:
CredentialStore saves the user's email and plaintext password in SharedPreferences when 'Remember me' is on (the default).
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/CredentialStore.kt:12: Password stored unencrypted in SharedPreferences 'credentials'.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0233: Hardcoded HTTP URLs
findings.explanation:
Receipt thumbnails are downloaded from a hardcoded http:// URL through the authenticated ApiClient, and the network security config allows cleartext.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/Endpoints.kt:6: Hardcoded HTTP base URL.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/ui/ThumbnailCache.kt:25: Used for a real download (bearer token attached by AuthInterceptor).

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0235: Android App Configurations Allowing Cleartext Traffic
findings.explanation:
The network security config's base-config permits cleartext traffic for every domain.
app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:3: base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0282: Unsafe Custom Trust Evaluation
findings.explanation:
UploadClient installs a custom X509TrustManager whose checkServerTrusted is empty and getAcceptedIssuers returns an empty array, so it accepts any certificate for receipt image uploads.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:19: Trust manager accepts every server certificate.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0283: Incorrect Implementation of Server Hostname Verification
findings.explanation:
UploadClient's HostnameVerifier always returns true.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:28: Hostname verification disabled.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0226: Debuggable Flag Enabled in the AndroidManifest
findings.explanation:
The release build type sets isDebuggable to true.
app/build.gradle.kts:23: isDebuggable = true

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0227: Debugging Enabled for WebViews
findings.explanation:
WebView debugging is enabled unconditionally in Application.onCreate, with no FLAG_DEBUGGABLE check.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/PennyJarApp.kt:45: Unconditional WebView debugging.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0334: Native Code Exposed Through WebViews
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity enables JavaScript and exposes HelpBridge.sessionToken() to any page; the page URL comes unvalidated from an exported deep link, so any site can read the session token.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:28: JS bridge registered on the WebView.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpBridge.kt:14: Bridge returns the session token to JavaScript.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:43: Untrusted URL loaded into the bridged WebView.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0254: Dangerous App Permissions
findings.explanation:
Place tagging only needs a one-off foreground city lookup (NETWORK_PROVIDER, locality), yet the app requests fine and background location; background location is asked for right after foreground is granted. Ward's analyzer said: Dangerous (runtime) permissions requested. Check that each is needed for a feature, and that a weaker one (coarse instead of fine location, foreground instead of background) would not do.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:8: Background location declared with no background feature.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/ui/AddExpenseScreen.kt:81: Background location requested at runtime.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:6: android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:8: android.permission.ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9: android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0318: References to SDK APIs Known to Handle Sensitive User Data
findings.explanation:
Mixpanel identify() gets the user's email and track() gets merchant names. Tracking starts at app start, and the stored analytics consent is never checked.

app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:22: Merchant name sent with each expense event.

findings.title: MASWE-0068: Incorrect Use of Identifiers for User Tracking
findings.explanation:
The user's email address is used as the Mixpanel tracking identifier.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:14: PII used as tracking ID.

findings.explanation:

findings.title: MASWE-0076: Lack of Proper Data Management Controls
findings.explanation:
Users can create an account here, but Ward found no way to delete it: no delete-account code, text or link in the scanned files. Google Play requires apps that allow account creation to offer an in-app path to delete the account and its data; a link to a web page counts (rule checked 2026-11-23, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13327111).
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/AuthRepository.kt:25: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:85: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:96: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:99: account creation
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:35: account creation

findings.title: MASWE-0078: Inadequate or Ambiguous User Consent Mechanisms
findings.explanation:
The consent screen stores the analytics choice, but Analytics never reads it: app_opened is tracked before consent is asked, and declining has no effect.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/PennyJarApp.kt:53: Tracking fires on every launch regardless of consent.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0200: Files Written to External Storage

Code writes an unencrypted expense CSV to public external storage; a run would show the file in Documents/PennyJar.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:24: Plaintext expense CSV written to public external storage.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0202: References to APIs and Permissions for Accessing External Storage
findings.explanation:
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared and AutoBackupWorker writes an unencrypted CSV of all expenses (dates, amounts, merchants, places) to the public Documents directory.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9: Shared-storage write permission declared.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:21: Backup target is the public Documents directory.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:24: Financial records written there as plaintext CSV.

findings.title: MASWE-0004: Sensitive Data Hardcoded in the App Package
findings.explanation:
A helpdesk API bearer token is hardcoded in SupportClient and shipped in the APK.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/support/SupportClient.kt:35: Helpdesk API secret hardcoded.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0216: Sensitive Data Not Excluded From Backup
findings.explanation:
Backup is on (android:allowBackup="true") and there are no backup rules (dataExtractionRules, fullBackupContent), so every app file goes into cloud backups and device transfers.

ApiClient adds OkHttp HttpLoggingInterceptor at Level.BODY (after AuthInterceptor), which logs login request bodies with email and password plus the Authorization bearer header to logcat.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:25: Full request/response bodies and headers logged.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:32: Login body with password goes through the logging client.
